P2-W01-T01.note: WorktreeManager (create/remove/list_registered) over real `git worktree` invocations -- first module in the crate with an external-process dependency rather than pure filesystem I/O. Isolation proven both directions (live-repo changes don't leak into a pinned attempt workspace; attempt-workspace writes never appear in the live repo) against real Git repositories, nothing mocked. Required failure-injection proof (Phase Manifest SS6.4, 'unexpected process exit'): remove_recovers_from_a_worktree_directory_deleted_out_from_under_git simulates a crash by deleting the worktree directory out-of-band and confirms clean recovery via prune. Explicitly does not implement baseline capture, reconciliation, or merge -- those are P2-W02+.

P2-W02-T01.note: Baseline::capture(workspace_root) walks a workspace and records a sha256 content hash per regular file keyed by relative path (Blueprint SS4.4's baseline shape), reusing event.rs's existing hex_encode rather than a second hashing convention. .git excluded regardless of file type -- caught a real gap during testing, not just a theoretical one: the main repo's .git is a directory but a `git worktree add` checkout's .git is a gitlink FILE, and the first implementation only excluded the directory form until the worktree-integration test (against a real P2-W01 AttemptWorkspace) caught .git leaking into the baseline. Fixed, plus a dedicated unit test added for the gitlink-file form specifically. Baseline::diff/diff_full report Added/Removed/Modified{before,after}/Unchanged per path -- the comparison primitive Invariant 13's live-workspace re-check and P2-W03's reconciliation will consume; this task does not implement either of those policies. Capture proven to be a pure read.

P2-W03-T01.note: ReconciliationOutcome reproduces Blueprint SS4.3's six-variant enum verbatim; reconcile(before, after, expected) -> ReconciliationOutcome is a pure deterministic function implementing algorithm steps 1-5 (NoChange/ExpectedChange/PartialChange/UnexpectedChange) over Baseline diffs (P2-W02). UserChangeDetected/Conflict are defined for spec-fidelity but never produced by reconcile() -- they require mutation attribution (P2-W05) and region-overlap detection (P2-W06) that do not exist yet; approximating them from file-level data alone would be false-confidence evidence. Restart-safety (Blueprint SS6) satisfied structurally: reconcile() has no internal state or I/O, so a crash mid-reconciliation just means calling it again against the same durable inputs -- proven by an explicit restart-safety test, not asserted. Return type has no path to AttemptStatus::Succeeded at all, upholding Invariant 14 by construction.

P2-W04-T01.note: recommended_attempt_status(outcome) -> Option<AttemptStatus> implements Blueprint SS4.3's outcome-to-next-action mapping: ExpectedChange -> None (defers to the not-yet-built Verification Engine; no AttemptStatus value in this crate means reconciliation-thinks-this-succeeded), every other outcome -> Some(Failed). State.rs's existing (P1) authorization gate restricting Running/Unknown->Succeeded to TransitionActor::VerificationEngine was NOT modified -- this task reinforces Invariant 14 by proving reconciliation cannot circumvent it. Required direct test (Phase Manifest SS6.3: reconciliation result != Succeeded transition) implemented exhaustively over all six outcome variants, plus a real integration test taking an actual reconcile() ExpectedChange result through try_attempt_transition across every TransitionActor, confirming only VerificationEngine is authorized.

P2-W05-T01.note: attribute_mutations(path, baseline, ai_result, live_current, expected) classifies line-regions into Blueprint SS4.6's four categories (ExpectedConductorChange/UnexpectedAiChange/UserChange/ConflictRegion) using two real `git diff --no-index` invocations anchored to the same baseline line numbers, not a custom diff algorithm -- consistent with the crate's established real-Git discipline (P2-W01). Reuses P2-W03's ExpectedOperation for the expected/unexpected file-scope decision rather than inventing a second concept. Pure-insertion hunks are conservatively widened to a single-line overlap window (documented and directly tested), so under-flagging a real conflict never happens at the cost of occasionally over-flagging one -- the safe direction per Invariant 11. Does not implement the conflict-halt policy (P2-W06) or how a real caller obtains the three snapshots from a running attempt (P2-W07/Phase 5) -- both explicitly out of scope.

P2-W06-T01.note: check_merge_safety(original_baseline, live_at_merge_time) implements Invariant 13's merge-time re-check via Baseline::diff, counting only Modified/Removed paths as drift -- Added paths excluded per Blueprint SS5.1's table row for newly-created untracked files, proven by a dedicated test. decide_merge(merge_check, attributions) combines that signal with P2-W05's ConflictRegion signal; Proceed is reachable in exactly one of the four combinations, proven by an exhaustive sweep, not inferred from testing each signal alone. Halt carries real evidence (changed paths / conflicting regions), not a bare flag. Deliberately does not drive any MissionStatus transition -- state.rs has no actor-authorization wrapper for mission-level transitions yet (confirmed by grep before writing code, unlike P2-W04 which had try_attempt_transition ready to compose against) -- nor the four-way person decision UI (P2-W07), nor the merge write itself, nor the mutation lock.

P2-W07-T01.note: PersonDecision reproduces Blueprint SS4.3's four-way choice verbatim (KeepUserVersion/KeepAiVersion/Merge/ReviewDiff) -- no fifth auto-resolve option, Invariant 11 upheld by construction. describe_conflict/render_decision_prompt surface real evidence (paths, region ranges), proven present in output, not generic text. record_person_decision mirrors console.rs's request_attempt_cancellation exactly (same StorePaths/EventLog/NewEvent path, caller-supplied now_ms, no direct clock read per AC-12) and writes the decision plus the evidence it responds to. Deliberately does not execute the chosen resolution (no merge write -- the mutation lock and merge-executor remain unbuilt, same P2-W06 scope boundary) and does not drive any MissionStatus transition (still no authorization wrapper for that in state.rs).

P3-W01-T01.note: ProviderRequest/ProviderResult reproduce Blueprint SS10.1's thickened fields (capability_snapshot/raw_metadata/sanitized_metadata as serde_json::Value passthroughs -- SS10.3's full capability-registry shape is not this task's job to design). FakeBehavior reproduces SS10.2's ten variants verbatim. FakeProvider is script-driven (FIFO push_behavior/send), fails closed on an empty script (ScriptExhausted) rather than defaulting to Success, and DuplicateResponse replays the actual prior successful result rather than fabricating one (fails closed via NoDuplicateAvailable if none exists). SlowResponse's Duration is recorded as data (simulated_delay), never slept on -- no direct clock use (AC-12). Deliberate, flagged deviation from Blueprint SS10.1: send() is synchronous, not async -- no async runtime exists anywhere in this crate yet and introducing one is a bigger architectural decision than this task should make unilaterally; documented in the module and contract for whichever future task wires in a real network-bound adapter.

P3-W02-T01.note: Clock trait (now_ms/source) plus RealClock (the crate's one sanctioned SystemTime::now() call, confirmed by crate-wide grep audit) and VirtualClock (AtomicU64-backed, starts at a caller-chosen value, advances exactly and instantly via advance(Duration) -- Blueprint SS28.5's 'clock advances 30s' made concrete). Both implement Clock and were proven usable interchangeably through a &dyn Clock trait object. Deliberately did not retrofit console.rs/person_decision.rs to take a Clock parameter -- both already correctly avoid direct clock reads via caller-supplied now_ms, and reopening two already-ACCEPTED modules wasn't required by the hard rule (which governs who may read the clock, not every function's parameter shape).

P3-W03-T01.note: ChaosCategory reproduces Blueprint SS10.4's eight categories verbatim with exact default weights (10/10/5/15/5/5/5/5). ChaosConfig carries chaos_seed/scenario_id/virtual_time_seed per SS10.4's hard rule. ChaosEngine::roll evaluates each category as an independent trial via a self-contained splitmix64 PRNG (no new randomness dependency), proven deterministic across repeated seeded runs. Four provider-layer categories map to FakeBehavior (P3-W01); ProcessTermination/CheckpointInterruption/StatePersistenceInterruption deliberately have no mechanical mapping yet -- no attempt-execution orchestrator exists for them to interrupt. simulate_user_edit_mid_attempt (Phase Manifest's explicitly required category) is proven, end to end, to trigger P2-W06's Conflict detection -- composing P2-W02/P2-W06/P3-W03 into one real passing test, not just existing as an enum variant.

P3-W04-T01.note: Scenario/ScenarioStep are the Rust shape of Blueprint SS28.4's YAML DSL (Scenario derives serde Serialize/Deserialize for future file loading; behavior is #[serde(skip)] since FakeBehavior isn't itself serde-derived yet -- documented, not silently assumed). run_scenario actually executes: real temp workspace, real setup files, real Baseline capture, steps run in order with a failing ProviderBehavior genuinely stopping remaining steps, real reconcile() AND real check_merge_safety(). Bug found and fixed during this session's own verification (not papered over): the first version only called reconcile(), which cannot see that an 'expected' file was changed by a user rather than the attempt -- changed_baseline_family failed cargo test for real, exposing that changed-baseline/merge-conflict/user-conflict are fundamentally about Invariant 13's merge-time re-check, not reconcile() alone. Fixed by having the engine run both real checks and scenarios assert on whichever is relevant. Blueprint's own worked example (timeout_after_partial_edit) reproduced and proven to produce PartialChange. All 17 of Phase Manifest SS7.4's required failure families covered by real, executed, asserted scenarios, with every non-obvious mapping (5xx->Crash, quota exhaustion, ambiguous outcome->Timeout, the three abort-marker categories) documented explicitly in code rather than left implicit.

P4-W01-T01.note: SECURITY-SCOPE WARNING (repeated in module/contract/report on purpose): VerificationStage implements Blueprint SS7's eight-stage pipeline with genuine short-circuiting (proven directly). RequirementVerificationClass implements SS7's three classes verbatim; ModelAssisted structurally cannot alone satisfy a blocking requirement. run_verification_command implements FOUR of SS7.1's sandbox protections for real against real process execution (command allowlist, working-directory confinement, a real timeout via poll-loop, environment-variable filtering via env_clear) plus mutation detection reusing P2-W02's Baseline -- but does NOT implement OS-level process-tree containment (job objects/namespaces/cgroups) or network isolation, both explicitly deferred to a dedicated future task with its own escape-attempt test suite. P4-W02-T01.note: Evidence implements Blueprint SS4.5's structured provenance record. EvidenceProvenance (6 variants) and Reproducibility (Deterministic|Flaky|Unknown) reproduced verbatim; ObservationType and IntegrityLevel are explicitly flagged as this task's own minimal interpretation since Blueprint doesn't enumerate their variants anywhere read for this task. produced_at_ms stored instead of a literal freshness Duration (a fixed Duration captured once would go stale) -- freshness always computed on demand against a caller-supplied now_ms, zero direct clock reads (grep-audited). matches(provenance, max_freshness, execution_id, now_ms) proven to fail independently on wrong provenance, staleness, wrong execution_id, and a failed underlying result -- four separate tests, not one combined case. from_stage_outcome connects real P4-W01 StageOutcome results to real Evidence, including the SkippedDueToEarlierFailure edge case correctly mapping to result:false.

P4-W03-T01.note: VerificationType reproduces exactly Blueprint SS8's five named verification types; ExpectedResult::Other(String) flagged as this task's own fallback beyond the single shown exit_code_0 example. Criterion/MissionAcceptanceContract/RequiredEvidenceSpec match SS8's JSON shape field-for-field; RequiredEvidenceSpec reuses P4-W02's EvidenceProvenance directly. evaluate_contract reuses Evidence::matches (P4-W02) directly rather than re-implementing provenance/freshness comparison. Missing evidence for a criterion fails explicitly (NoEvidenceProvided), distinguishable from EvidenceDidNotMatch -- proven as separate outcomes, not assumed. all_blocking_satisfied() ignores non-blocking criteria, proven against a case built to look identical to a failing-blocking case if that distinction were dropped. Blueprint's own seven-criterion 'auth' worked example reproduced and evaluated end to end. Never references AttemptStatus anywhere in its logic (grep-audited) -- setting Succeeded remains explicitly P4-W04's job. P4-W04-T01.note: decide() composes P4-W01's pipeline result, P4-W03's MAC evaluation, and two additional checks (wrong-verification-method via observation_type vs verification_type; false-model-success via requiring IntegrityLevel::IndependentlyVerified for blocking criteria, mirroring P4-W01's ModelAssisted rule) into one SuccessDecision. Neither P4-W02 nor P4-W03 was reopened -- both additions are this task's own layer on top, explicitly flagged as interpretation beyond Blueprint SS8's literal JSON schema. attempt_succeeded_transition calls the REAL state::try_attempt_transition(VerificationEngine, Running, Succeeded) exactly once, only in the Succeed branch. All 8 of Phase Manifest SS8.4's required scenarios (passing/failing acceptance criteria, stale evidence, insufficient evidence, wrong verification method, partial completion, false model success, favorable-reconciliation-without-verification) proven as individual named tests; the passing scenario proven against a REAL Ok(()) from the actual state.rs gate, not simulated. Crate-wide grep audit confirms verification_engine.rs is the only production call site anywhere in the crate that calls try_attempt_transition with a Succeeded target -- closes Invariant 14's proof chain end to end (P1's structural gate -> P2-W04's reconciliation-alone-can't-do-it confirmation -> this task's full-composed-engine confirmation).
